schema_forms.protocol_object: An independently versioned protocol object: its own schema version, canonical bytes and object hash.
schema_forms.embedded_contract_part: A part frozen inside a contract. It is versioned with the contract that embeds it and enters that contract's identity tiers; it has no identity of its own (U-42 asks how other objects reference it).
schema_forms.ledger_state_row: A ledger row changed only by compare-and-swap transitions. Its schema is versioned with the ledger, not exchanged as a protocol object.
schema_forms.append_only_journal_record: An immutable fact appended to a ledger journal and never changed after it is written.
schema_forms.raw_witness: The producer's exact bytes, kept unchanged. Autobot defines only how it is admitted (U-21) and parsed (U-41).
schema_forms.legacy_read_only: Imported history. Readable, never authoritative under v1 rules unless re-verified (D-07).

authority_effects.contract: Frozen requirement; defines what must be proven.
authority_effects.proof: Authoritative receipt; may count toward finalization and acceptance.
authority_effects.state: Authoritative lifecycle state, changed only by the Sequencer's transitions.
authority_effects.evidence_only: Evidence for admission; never authority by itself (R-7, R-9).
authority_effects.none: Grants nothing. It records a fact a transition may require (t-a02 requires the dispatch projection), but a parser must never let it satisfy an acceptance, finalization or evidence requirement.
authority_effects.legacy: Read-only history; grants nothing under v1 rules.

canonical_hash_forms.object_hash: A hash over the object's canonical bytes. Its construction, including whether it carries a domain label or a type binding, is open (U-28, U-30, U-53).
canonical_hash_forms.within_tiers: No hash of its own; its canonical value enters the parent contract's identity tiers.
canonical_hash_forms.by_id_and_version: Referenced by identifier and version; no object hash is required in v1.
canonical_hash_forms.hash_chain: Each entry hashes its predecessor (append-only hash chain).
canonical_hash_forms.content_sha256: SHA-256 of exact bytes, as content address (U-29).
canonical_hash_forms.undecided: Chapter 0 sets no identity policy; see the object's unknowns.

creation_forms.note: created_by is recorded for each object whose minter is a transition actor in transitions.json (the Sequencer or the Registry) but which no Chapter 0 transition mints. It cites Chapter 0's lifecycle text and never names a transition as the minter.
creation_forms.lifecycle_coupling: Created one for one with another object, by a Chapter 0 invariant.
creation_forms.lifecycle_rule: Created as Chapter 0's lifecycle text says.

binding_conditions.binding_set: BindingSet(record) = common_bindings ∪ the bindings of every conditional rule whose complete when predicate holds for the record. Rules add up: a record that matches several rules inherits the bindings of all of them. A record is immutable after commitment (R-2), so its set is fixed when it is produced, and every transition that later consumes it sees that same set.
binding_conditions.common_bindings: Bound in every context the object appears in.
binding_conditions.conditional_bindings: Binding rules, each {when, provenance, bindings, open}. Within one rule, every selector in when must hold (AND), and a list of values in one selector means any of them. Across rules, every rule that holds contributes its bindings. A rule with no bindings records explicitly that it adds nothing. An open rule is one whose bindings Chapter 0 leaves open; it cites the unknown that asks.
binding_conditions.partitions: Rules conditioned on the same selectors form one partition: obj-30 has a path partition and a finalization_class partition, and obj-26 one partition on path, effect and effect_result. Within each partition every Chapter 0 context of the record resolves to exactly one rule; across partitions the matches add up (inventory.contexts). So an RO AcceptanceReceipt matches the RO rule and the READ_ONLY rule, and inherits both.
binding_conditions.provenance: The Chapter 0 transitions a rule covers: those that mint, prove or consume the record in a context its when clause matches. t-s16 proves the SL canonical commit, and t-s20 later consumes that receipt without performing the effect. Provenance is not a selector and not a wire field: it never decides whether a rule holds, so a record's bindings never depend on which transition consumes it. Where a rule lists it, the list is exact (inventory.provenance).

selectors.path: a finalization path or path group (transitions.json paths)
selectors.effect: the effect the record is the receipt or the intent of (transitions.json effects). For a receipt this is the effect it records, as the transition that established the receipt says; a later consumer such as t-s20 doesn't perform it.
selectors.effect_result: what happened to that effect (effect_results); not an EffectIntent state
selectors.kind: a record kind of a multi-kind object

effect_results.note: What happened to the effect a receipt records, as the Chapter 0 transition whose own preconditions establish it says (t-s16, t-s17, t-s18). A later consumer (t-s20) takes the result from that transition. These are not EffectIntent states: the six states of states.json are unchanged.

HAPPENED.meaning: the effect happened: the target is at the new value

EXPECTED_OLD_STALE.meaning: the compare-and-swap found the ref moved, so its expected old value is stale and the effect didn't happen

ponr_only_bindings.rule: Bound only where the receipt records a point of no return that happened. Every such receipt binds the delegation state, and also the consumed reservation where the point of no return consumes one. Both come from the transition that established the receipt, so a later consumer sees the same receipt: t-s20 sees t-s16's.

source_state.meaning: the exact source or subject state

candidate_tree.meaning: the candidate source tree of a source-modifying contract

artifact_set.meaning: the candidate artifacts, under the contract's artifact paths

assertion_ids.meaning: the assertions checked; they are embedded in the contract, so how they are referenced is open

delegation_state_at_ponr.meaning: the delegation's state, frozen into the receipt at the point of no return

delegation_active_at_intent.meaning: the delegation was active when the intent committed

reservation_held.meaning: the permit-use reservation held while the intent is live: taken entering COMMITTING (permit_reserved), held into a publication or retry intent (reservation_held), or taken afresh when a halted remote verification resumes (t-s29)

reservation_consumed.meaning: the permit-use reservation, consumed at this point of no return

reservation_released.meaning: the permit-use reservation, released on an exit before the point of no return

ref_values.meaning: the target ref with its expected old and new values

effect_outcome.meaning: the outcome observed under the effect's outcome rule

intent_window.meaning: the intent's window and hard timeout

intent.meaning: the EffectIntent the effect ran under

committed_tree.meaning: the committed tree, equal to the verified tree

checked_commit.meaning: the exact commit the remote check ran on

observation_window.meaning: the observation window of a READ_ONLY acceptance

edge_target.meaning: the edge's required target: one specific TaskContractRecord, or any record with the same ContractDigest or RequirementDigest, satisfied by the declared tier

permit_source.meaning: the permit whose uses it counts: a standing permit a delegation carries, or a per-sequence PublicationPermit

input_rehash.meaning: the specification inputs' hashes recomputed at collection and compared with the contract's; a change is INTEGRITY_FAILED

record_hash_and_digest.meaning: the record hash and the digest

admitted_witness_hashes.meaning: content hashes of the admitted witnesses

reuse_conditions.meaning: the six preconditions of reuse at admission and once ready

INV-28: CH1-scope-check needs its scope fields

ch1_scope_reason: CLOSURE §6: the registration and transform schemas

objects.name: TaskContractRecord (three identity tiers, resolved bindings)
ch1_scope_reason: CLOSURE §6: golden hashes for all three identity tiers
objects.note: A freeze you author has no delegation (D-11), so the delegation binding can be absent (U-37, U-40).

objects.name: DependencyEdge (required record, contract or requirement)
objects.note: One type whose target is a specific record, the same contract, or the same requirement, plus an observation requirement (CORR-21). Only a record-level edge names one TaskContractRecord; a contract- or requirement-level edge names a digest that any matching record's acceptance can satisfy (INV-09). Other objects reference an edge without it having a hash of its own (U-42).

objects.name: Sequence
ch1_scope_reason: the ledger state model is Chapter 2

created_by.rule: Exactly one Sequence exists for each TaskContractRecord (INV-40), so a Sequence comes into being with every new record (ARCHITECTURE §7); a duplicate admission creates none (INV-54). No Chapter 0 transition mints it: t-c02 and t-c05 mint only the record and its embedded parts.

ch1_scope_reason: the dispatch projection and the role-transform check are Chapters 3 and 4

objects.name: CandidateReceipt
ch1_scope_reason: candidates are Chapter 4: artifact sets first, then source trees
objects.note: Every contract has artifact paths in its RequirementDigest (identity.json), so every candidate binds its artifact set; a source-modifying candidate also binds its tree.

objects.name: ActualVerificationEnvironment
ch1_scope_reason: U-10: environment capture for Python verifiers is resolved inside Chapter 1

objects.name: RemoteVerificationReceipt
objects.note: Before publication (SRP) the check runs on the staged commit; after publication (SRPO) on the canonical one.

objects.name: PublicationPermit (per-sequence grant)
ch1_scope_reason: permit accounting is Chapter 2; publication is Chapter 6

created_by.rule: Counts the uses of one publication permit: a standing permit a delegation carries (D-03), or a per-sequence permit (obj-22), which ARCHITECTURE §9 tracks as a one-use permit state from its grant. Only the Sequencer changes it (INV-48). No Chapter 0 transition creates it; the permit counters are Chapter 2's ledger work (ARCHITECTURE §17).

objects.name: EffectIntent
ch1_scope_reason: intent rows are Chapter 2; outcome rules are Chapter 6
objects.note: Six states in Chapter 0 (states.json effect_intent): PENDING, HAPPENED, ABSENT, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, SUPERSEDED_BY_RETRY, HUMAN_RESOLVED. The two standalone effects need an intent, but no transition creates one (U-44). t-i06 mints a retry intent for the identical effect outside any initiation rule. Chapter 0 gives no field that marks a retry, so the retry falls under its effect's rule and would bind the attempt, the delegation at intent and the intent window, none of which t-i06 checks: no fence_matches, no delegation_active_at_intent, and no intent_ttl_gt_hard_timeout (U-47, RV-50, RV-52). Both are Chapter 0 correction candidates.

objects.name: CommitReceipt
objects.note: Produced for two effects: the SL canonical commit, which t-s16 proves at the point of no return, and the REMOTE sequence-scoped ref, which t-s17 proves (not a point of no return). t-s18 consumes it when the compare-and-swap found the ref already moved, so committed_tree holds only when the effect happened. t-s20 performs no effect: it consumes the receipt t-s16 established and sees the same bindings. The consumed reservation and the delegation state hold only when eff-local-canonical-cas happened on SL; the receipt t-s18 consumes records a released reservation instead (RV-25, applied by RV-48, with provenance kept apart by RV-49). The common bindings carry the attempt, the intent and the ref facts: the expected old and new values (ref_values) and the observed outcome (effect_outcome).

objects.name: PublicationReceipt
objects.note: Required only after the canonical push happened (t-s33, always a point of no return; then t-s37), so its bindings are common. If a push that didn't happen also gets one (INV-43, U-48), the delegation state and the consumed reservation move into an effect_result context, as for the CommitReceipt.

objects.name: AcceptanceReceipt
objects.note: Minted on all seven paths. It is the point-of-no-return receipt only on RO, RUD and RUR; on SL and the REMOTE paths it follows an earlier one. It also binds every receipt its finalization requirements name (ARCHITECTURE §13). Chapter 0 doesn't make it attempt-bound: on the execution paths its minting transitions check the fence (t-s14, t-s20, t-s37, t-s39), and it carries the attempt only through the attempt-bound receipts it binds. Reuse paths have no attempt.

objects.name: FulfillmentReuseReceipt (dominance proof)
objects.note: Binds the requesting record and the earlier acceptance it reuses. Minted only at the reuse points of no return (t-s43, t-s44), so its bindings are common.

objects.name: DuplicateAdmissionRecord
ch1_scope_reason: INV-40: CH1-duplicate-admission produces it (t-c03 mints obj-32)
objects.note: Chapter 0 sets no identity policy for it: whether it is referenced by an identifier or by a hash waits on U-22 and U-30.

objects.name: ForwardRepairObligation
ch1_scope_reason: forward repair after PUBLISHED_UNVERIFIED is Chapter 6
objects.note: t-o02 consumes the repair's AcceptanceReceipt to reach RESOLVED. Whether the row then records it is part of the Chapter 2 ledger state model (ARCHITECTURE §17), so it isn't listed as a binding.

objects.name: TransitionRecord
ch1_scope_reason: the journal and failpoints are Chapter 2

created_by.rule: Appended to the hash-chained journal for every transition the Sequencer applies (ARCHITECTURE §15, cap-51), so that replay reproduces the same next state (INV-10). It records each transition rather than being the mint of any one.

objects.name: ManualAttestation (kind ASSERTION or EFFECT_OUTCOME)
ch1_scope_reason: HUMAN_REQUIRED acceptance is Chapter 5; effect outcomes are Chapter 6 (t-i07)

objects.name: SupersessionRecord / AbandonRecord
ch1_scope_reason: supersession and abandonment fence in-flight attempts in Chapter 2 (w-s02, w-s03)
supersession_provenance in the RecordHash refers to supersession (U-52)

created_by.rule: Held by the one running Sequencer instance in the interim topology (ARCHITECTURE §15, INV-25a, cap-49); t-s06 requires it held. No Chapter 0 transition acquires it, and Chapter 0 names no trigger beyond the single-instance rule; acquiring and renewing the lease is Chapter 2's ledger work (ARCHITECTURE §17).
